mbm-2426.clue: My sewing needles sleep in a boot.
mbm-2426.quote: I shaped scraps of leather into a thimble-sized work boot to hold needles. My niece added yellow laces. It now sits by my real boots whenever she visits.

mbm-2427.clue: I can juggle a rain shower.
mbm-2427.quote: I learned with three blue scarves on the porch. One windy day the scarves sailed toward my grandpa in a lovely row. He raised his umbrella and applauded my forecast.

mbm-2428.clue: Our subtitles wear out a chalkboard.
mbm-2428.quote: We watch one scene from a tape over and over and invent new dialogue for it. My sister brought a tiny chalkboard to change the ending without talking over anybody's favorite song.

mbm-2429.clue: I recognize a museum by its floorboards.
mbm-2429.quote: I sketch the feet of visitors standing near sculptures. Last Sunday all my sketches had little red booties. It had started pouring and the guard had handed them out to save the parquet.

mbm-2430.quote: My niece puts her rubber duck in the bow of my canoe facing me. When we pass the reeds she whispers all the birds she thinks the duck has spotted. We travel very well as three.

mbm-2431.clue: The net leaves a map on my palm.
mbm-2431.quote: I mend our beach volleyball net with green cord. Every time I loop it over my hand I can feel where last year's storm tore it. The green patch is where my friends aim their serves.

mbm-2432.clue: I keep a spare sunset in the cupboard.
mbm-2432.quote: I juggle three painted wooden balls, red, orange and purple. My little sister calls it evening when I throw them high. Before bed I put the sunset back above the plates.

mbm-2433.clue: The dinosaur's tail gets a day off.
mbm-2433.quote: Our mini-golf dinosaur lost the tip of its tail. I drew the missing piece on my scorecard and held it up for the group picture. The owner framed our photo beside the till.

mbm-2434.clue: My sister gets first turn on the broken button.
mbm-2434.quote: The jump button sticks on our old arcade stick. My sister can free it with a tap from her smallest finger. We play doubles so her tiny rescue can save my hero midair.

mbm-2435.clue: My prize ribbon has flour on both ends.
mbm-2435.quote: At the doughnut contest I won by half a bite. Dad held up one end of my ribbon while Mum held the other. Both forgot they had powdered fingers. Our family got a ribbon in its own colors.

mbm-2436.clue: I need two handkerchiefs for the shyest spectator.
mbm-2436.quote: At a party a small girl wouldn't take a card. I made one silk vanish and pulled its twin from her dad's jacket. She asked if handkerchiefs could trade places again on the way home.

mbm-2437.clue: One of the dice is always upstairs.
mbm-2437.quote: I built a little dice tower from my kid brother's blocks. Now when I roll, the dice tumble past a tiny paper family he drew in the windows. He insists they pay rent in jellybeans.

mbm-2438.clue: My left shoe knows which lane squeaks.
mbm-2438.quote: The old bowling alley creaks on lane four. I can hear my mother's approach even with my back to her. On her birthday the staff let her bowl the first ball there by herself.

mbm-2439.clue: The windmill has a birthday candle.
mbm-2439.quote: Dad always missed the windmill hole. When he finally made it I stuck a candle in the cupcake we'd brought. The blades blew it out before he got his wish, so he got another turn.

mbm-2440.clue: We had to weigh my napkin.
mbm-2440.quote: A watermelon seed contest got tangled up with the pie contest next door. My napkin ended up full of seeds and purple crust. I lost on both tables and still went home happy.

mbm-2441.clue: I gave the smallest passenger the front seat.
mbm-2441.quote: A gust rolled my spare wool hat off the dock and right into my kayak. I left it tucked in the bow. By lunchtime a little tree frog was riding the folded cuff. I pulled alongside the reeds so it could get off at its stop.

mbm-2442.clue: I took one family portrait with my eyes shut.
mbm-2442.quote: I set my old camera timer and ran. Just as it clicked, Dad tickled my neck. My eyes are closed in the print and everyone else is looking at me. That's the one on the wall.

mbm-2443.quote: I pick one faded sign in every town and follow it. A peeling blue arrow took me to a tiny carousel behind a bakery. I rode the painted goat twice before lunch.

mbm-2444.quote: I cut a pair of red paper shutters for my father's shop window. When he unlocks the real shutters, he opens the little paper ones too. Peep through and you can see a paper cat in his paper shop, sitting exactly where the real one sits.

mbm-2445.clue: The last frame belongs to the fence.
mbm-2445.quote: I take the same photo of our neighbor's garden fence each season. The paint keeps peeling, but that one sunflower gets taller than the gate in every summer print.

mbm-2446.clue: My canoe has a penny for the crossing.
mbm-2446.quote: I fitted a small coin into a shallow nick in the old wooden thwart. Whenever we pass the toll bridge above I tap it for luck. So far nobody has charged us another penny.

mbm-2447.clue: I listen to the ninth pin.
mbm-2447.quote: I made one spare with a long hollow clonk. The man who oils our bowling lanes called it a clean note. He gave me a little brass bell for my bag. It rings off key and I love it.
